Comment: Interesting and fun

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Fun Reverse clash :) Simple and easy to understand and implement

Cases
* There are currently no tests where the initial # is close to, but not at, either end (of the ground?). Please modify Proliferation (Test 7) so that it becomes a mirrored version of Validator 7, using a different [[d]].

* What about an input of the form [some dots]##[some dots]?

Thanks.

Hi 5DN1L!
As always, great advice :)

Validator 7 has been mirrored.

& Added 4 pairs of tests:
- Affected borders 
- Grouped Infections
- Asymmetry of the edges
- Global Pandemic (for stress)

Adding on to the cases coverage as started by @5DN1L:

- Any plans for adding cases where there are no '#' characters?

- It would be nice to have input lengths gradually increase and lead up to the final test case (Global Pandemic)

- Please add some test cases where the input string is made up of a decent number (e.g. >=40%) of '#' characters, for stress testing.

Also, may I suggest including the length of the input string as part of the input itself? This helps players using languages that don't support input parsing very well.

Thank you :)
Good suggestions, thanks, I'll do that! :)

I'm fine either way on whether long-string inputs are tested. However, aside from the cases that are specifically intended to hint at the required task, the cases should show a more gradual increase in [[d]], length of [[t]], and the number of # in [[t]]. Right now, there's a large jump from a short string with a few # to a very long string containing just one #.

Also, please remember to renumber the validators after reordering or inserting cases.

Thanks.

Thank you both for the feedback! I've reviewed all the test cases:
- Length is now included in the input
- The test cases have been reordered to show a gradual increase in D, length, and the number of #. I've added intermediate test cases to eliminate the abrupt jump to “Global Pandemic.”
- I’ve added cases with no #s at all and dense cases (≥40% #s) for the stress test.

Please let me know if you spot any other gaps. Thanks! :)
